statement_summary: Maintain a documented security program
Owner designated security and privacy lead in writing
Annual risk assessment using SP 800-30
Risk decision rules; High risks never accepted as they are
Annual self-assessment with periodic outside review
Policy reviewed at least every 12 months
Policy acknowledgment and confidentiality agreement before contractor access
Exceptions and changes logged and time-limited
No terms, no customer data (confidentiality, no training, deletion, breach notice)
Vendor list with data held and notice terms; processor marked as the account data provider
Terms check before new services; annual SOC 2 and P2PE listing review
Remove access and request deletion when a relationship ends
Named accounts; no shared logins; fill-in account disabled between cover periods
MFA on every service holding customer data or money
Unique passphrases; default passwords changed before use
Fill-in account without export rights; quarterly user and session review
Device lock times
Sealed emergency access codes and device-return procedure
Monthly review of sign-ins, exports, and connected devices
Three-level classification
Passcodes only in the restricted field cleared at release; no account passwords collected
Customer device access rules (good-faith access only)
Encrypted storage and 14-day deletion of transfer and recovery copies
SP 800-88 Rev. 2 sanitization methods with verification
Per-device sanitization record for recycling drop-offs
Card numbers only in the P2PE terminal; never written down or typed elsewhere
Paper intake forms shredded after one year; security records kept 5 years
Bench rules: screen and camera placement; scan customer drives; standard account
Updates, antivirus, and approved software sources only
Terminal list, weekly inspection, and service visitor checks
Guest and bench networks separated from shop devices
Annual training; PIM read; payment change call-back
AI tools only after assessment, on no-training terms, with no customer personal data
Customer-facing privacy, wiping, and AI statements must be true
Incident runbook with printed contacts
Same-day incident log with discovery time
Processor told within 24 hours of a suspected card data compromise
Meet Florida and other states' notice deadlines
No ransom without counsel and an OFAC check
Storm procedure
Monthly SYS-01 export and second copy of open recovery jobs
